title: Agent Route Tracking: Log, Analyze, and Optimize Pointer Traversals
purpose: Standard procedure for agents to log which pointer network paths they follow, and for coordinators to analyze route patterns to optimize the pointer network over time.

strength_levels.description: Every SCR/TOOL <-> SOP pointer has a strength classification guiding agents.

primary.meaning: This tool IS the SOP's implementation. The SOP directly names and uses it.
primary.agent_action: Use first. This is the canonical tool for this workflow.

supporting.meaning: This tool supports the SOP's workflow (monitoring, coordination, validation).
supporting.agent_action: Use when primary tool needs orchestration or post-processing.

related.meaning: Shares domain/tags but isn't directly used by the SOP.
related.agent_action: Consider for adjacent tasks or extending the SOP's scope.

agent_log_route.title: Log a Route During Task Execution
agent_log_route.when: An agent follows pointer network links to find tools, SOPs, or resources for a task.

steps.action: Track which nodes you traverse during task execution
steps.detail: As you follow pointers from an SOP to scripts, or from scripts to sources, record the chain of node IDs in order.

required_fields.task: Task category (e.g., wikipedia-enrichment, data-gathering, monitoring, coordination-setup, stress-test, indexing)
required_fields.route: Space-separated node IDs with ' -> ' between them

coordinator_analyze.title: Analyze Route Patterns
coordinator_analyze.when: After a multi-agent session, or periodically to optimize the pointer network.

check: strength_effectiveness: Are 'primary' routes succeeding more than 'related'?
top_edges: Which pointer links are most traversed?
outcome_distribution: What fraction of routes succeed?
recommended_route: Is the most common successful route the best one?
strengths_on_success: Which strength levels correlate with success?

recommend_route.title: Get Route Recommendation Before Starting a Task
recommend_route.when: An agent is about to start a task and wants to know the best pointer path.

steps.detail: Returns the historically best route if one exists, or falls back to strength-based suggestion from the pointer network.

steps.action: Follow the recommended route, but log your actual route when done (OP-01)

optimize_network.title: Use Route Data to Optimize Pointer Weights and Strengths
optimize_network.when: After accumulating 20+ route logs, or when success rates are below 70%.

steps.detail: If 'related' edges have higher success rates than 'primary' edges for a specific task, the pointer weights or strength classifications may need updating.
Edges that exist in the pointer network but are never traversed may indicate unnecessary connections. Consider removing or downgrading them.
If agents frequently traverse node pairs that DON'T have a direct pointer, add one. These are discovered shortcuts.

steps.action: Apply changes via SOP-028 (OP-06 for tag updates, OP-07 for full rebuild)

triggers: Success rate below 70% for any task type
New SOP or script added that changes routing landscape

view_top_routes.title: View Most-Used Routes from a Node
view_top_routes.when: Investigating which paths agents take from a specific SOP or script.

integration_with_agent_workflow.description: How agents should integrate route tracking into their normal workflow.
before_task: 3. Follow primary-strength pointers first, then supporting if needed
during_task: 1. Note each pointer you follow (node ID sequence)
2. If you deviate from the recommended route, note why
after_task: 2. If outcome was 'failure', include --notes explaining what went wrong
